company_posts.content:
Back in July I took Otani san and Yamazaki san down to Hambantota to visit the Lanka Salt saltern. We walked the pans at sunset, then spent the evening inside a few small processing centres nearby, tasting samples and talking to the people who run the machines.
 
We went with two questions.
 
Our Japanese partners were asking whether Sri Lankan salt, and what comes out alongside it, could feed beauty and personal care manufacturing in Japan. Gypsum settles in the concentrating ponds. Magnesium stays in the bittern left after harvest, the same raw material Japan knows as nigari. The pink colour in the crystalliser ponds comes from Dunaliella salina, a microalga whose carotenoid extracts already go into skincare. Most of it never leaves Hambantota as anything more than raw salt.
 
My own question was what a modern salt processing line would look like if we built it today, with sensors, embedded control and AI watching the evaporation, crystallisation and separation steps instead of relying on experience alone. The engineering is not the hard part. The hard part is that nobody has had the resources to try.
 
That gap is where SoftSora can be useful. We bring the technical side, AI, embedded systems and automation, and we bring the Japanese relationships that turn a pilot into a buyer. Ideas like this usually stall somewhere between the field and the factory. That is the part we are working on.
 
#SriLanka #Japan #AI #EmbeddedSystems #Manufacturing #Export #SoftSora

DWorld VR presents Touli, the new app born in Genoa to connect people, businesses, local shops, and the territory through a simple model: turning good actions into tangible value for the community.
Touli was created as the new mobile layer of the DWorld ecosystem. It does not replace the journey into the virtual cities we've built, but it will complement it with a more immediate, accessible tool that is closer to people’s everyday lives🌍 

The goal is to create a bridge between the real city and the virtual city, activating citizens, companies, associations, and local businesses around social, environmental, educational, sports, and wellbeing challenges.
The model is simple:
good actions → points → real gifts → value for the territory.
People who take part in positive activities can earn points and turn them into real gifts connected to the territory, while also helping support local historic shops and businesses🎁 
We chose to start from Genoa in Italy because it is a city with a strong identity, a rich economic and social fabric, and a network of historic businesses that represent a fundamental part of its community🇮🇹 

The project has received the endorsement of the Genoa Chamber of Commerce, and the first activities will begin in September 2026.
With Touli, we want to experiment with a new way of using technology: not only to create digital experiences, but to generate participation, relationships, and measurable social impact in the real world.
Genoa will be the first laboratory. Together with our partner SoftSora supporting our project , we'll share new markets shortly.
From here, the goal is to build a model capable of growing and involving new territories, new communities, and new businesses globally 🔜 

www.touli.ai

Last month we had the privilege of hosting Tomoaki Otani san, CEO of Frontieer Japan LLC, at our Colombo office for three weeks.

For anyone who knows the SoftSora story, Otani san is not just a business partner. He is one of the people who helped lay the foundation this company stands on today. Long before we had the team and the client base we have now across Japan and Europe, he believed in what a Sri Lankan team could deliver to Japanese enterprise standards.

Those three weeks were anything but a formal visit. Working sessions with our engineers. Deep dives into live projects. Honest feedback on quality, process and how Japanese clients think. Our team asked questions, challenged ideas and learned directly from someone who has spent his career building trust across two very different business cultures.

Seeing our younger engineers sit with him, some of them presenting to a Japanese client stakeholder for the first time, was the highlight of the month for all of us.

Otani san, thank you for the time, the honesty and the belief. The plaque our team put together says it better than words here can.

Here is to the next chapter of the Frontieer Japan and SoftSora partnership.

いつもありがとうございます。

As a university ranked among the top 1% globally, Curtin University's commitment to academic excellence is strengthened through close collaboration with industry, ensuring our programmes remain relevant, innovative, and future-focused.

We were delighted to host the Curtin University Colombo Industry Consultative Board – Computing 2026 on 24 July 2026 at Sofia Colombo City Hotel, bringing together leading technology industry professionals to help shape the future of computing education.

At Curtin University Colombo, we believe the best graduates are shaped by industry. The Industry Consultative Board serves as a vital platform connecting academia and industry, providing valuable insights into emerging technologies, employer expectations, graduate readiness, and the future skills required to succeed in an ever-evolving digital landscape.

The discussions focused on:
• Identifying emerging industry trends and graduate skill requirements
• Strengthening industry collaboration to enhance student learning and employability
• Reviewing and enhancing our computing curriculum to meet future workforce demands
• Creating stronger pathways between academia and industry

We extend our sincere appreciation to our valued industry representatives for sharing their expertise and insights:

Vipula Liyanaarachchi (Zone24x7), Erani Srikantha (IFS), Chandana Wijesuriya (Aeturnum), @Lasitha Weerasinghe(Aeturnum), Chamath Rathnasekara (Scybers), @Seshan Gamage (Wiley), Charuka Kaluarachchi (DOSCON AS), Udara Wijeratna (Velaris), @Lahiru Wijesekara (Nagarro), Madhusha Guruge (Dialog Axiata PLC ), Dinuka Samarakoon (Dialog Axiata PLC ), Dumindu Ranasinghearachchi (Dialog Axiata PLC), Niluksha Abeyruwan (SoftSora), Achintha Bandaranaike (MITESP), @Kasun Madhushanka (IFS), Kushan Yapa (Aeturnum), and Roshan Chandraguptha (Nagarro).

Your valuable contributions help us continuously enhance our computing programmes and ensure our students graduate with the knowledge, practical skills, and industry relevance needed to thrive in an ever-changing digital world.

Together with our industry partners, we are shaping the next generation of future-ready computing professionals.
